findings.title: Client-side rendering gap: raw HTML contains minimal text content
findings.evidence:
Observed at https://www.youtube.com/?feature=youtu.be via static_initial_html_shell_inspection [2026-09-13T15:44:49Z]: Raw HTML yields only 24 words of visible text and shows static shell signals (many-inline-or-external-scripts, markup-to-text-imbalance). Search crawlers and AI bots that do not execute client JS may not extract brand facts from this page. Other page-level checks were suppressed here: a missing heading, CTA, meta description or schema on an empty shell are all symptoms of this one root cause. (Confidence: medium)
Additional evidence (crawl-render-audit): Observed at https://www.youtube.com/ via static_initial_html_shell_inspection [2026-09-13T15:44:49Z]: Raw HTML yields only 24 words of visible text and shows static shell signals (many-inline-or-external-scripts, markup-to-text-imbalance). Search crawlers and AI bots that do not execute client JS may not extract brand facts from this page. Other page-level checks were suppressed here: a missing heading, CTA, meta description or schema on an empty shell are all symptoms of this one root cause. (Confidence: medium)

suggested_action.summary: Implement server-side rendering (SSR) or static pre-rendering for core content.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Use static site generation (SSG) or SSR so that primary textual facts and headers are present in initial HTTP responses without JS execution.
suggested_action.expected_benefit: Improves render gap by making the observed information clearer and more extractable for the intended audience.

findings.title: Brand identity is not anchored to any independent authority source
findings.evidence: Observed at https://www.youtube.com via onsite_identity_anchor_inspection [2026-09-13T15:44:53Z]: Across the crawled pages, Organization schema is present but declares 0 sameAs URIs, and 0 of 15 distinct outbound link domains point to an independent authority (Wikipedia, Wikidata, Crunchbase, LinkedIn, GitHub, regulatory registries). No explicit independent-authority link was observed in the sampled pages; external corroboration was not searched. (Confidence: medium)

suggested_action.summary: Publish machine-readable identity anchors linking the brand to independent authorities.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Add Organization JSON-LD with a stable @id, legalName, and a sameAs array pointing to the brand's Wikidata item, Wikipedia article, LinkedIn company page and Crunchbase profile. Create those external profiles first if they do not exist -- sameAs pointing at nothing does not corroborate anything.
suggested_action.expected_benefit: Improves corroboration by making the observed information clearer and more extractable for the intended audience.

findings.title: No returning-visitor or account affordance detected
findings.evidence: Observed at https://www.youtube.com via returning_visitor_affordance_detection [2026-09-13T15:44:49Z]: Across 5 crawled pages there is no sign-in, account, saved-items or recently-viewed affordance in the visible text. Every visitor is therefore treated as anonymous and first-time, so nothing the brand already knows about a returning visitor can shape what they are shown. (Confidence: medium)

suggested_action.summary: Give returning visitors a way to be recognised, and use it.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Add an account or saved-state affordance appropriate to the site (sign-in, saved items, recently viewed, or a lightweight preference stored locally), then use it to surface relevant content on return rather than resetting every visitor to a cold start.
suggested_action.expected_benefit: Improves personalization readiness by making the observed information clearer and more extractable for the intended audience.

evidence_details.observation: Across 5 crawled pages there is no sign-in, account, saved-items or recently-viewed affordance in the visible text. findings.title: No extractable answer on-site for "What makes YouTube different?"
findings.evidence: Observed at https://www.youtube.com/?feature=youtu.be via onsite_answerability_probe [2026-09-13T15:44:53Z]: Across 5 crawled page(s), no explicit differentiator or benefit statement is extractable from the relevant crawled pages. An assistant that fetched these pages could not quote an answer to "What makes YouTube different?" from this site, so it must fall back to third-party sources or omit the brand. (Confidence: medium)

suggested_action.summary: Make the brand's differentiator explicit and quotable.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Add a short, factual differentiator section tied to a specific capability, audience, outcome, or proof point.
suggested_action.expected_benefit: Improves citation omission by making the observed information clearer and more extractable for the intended audience.

proactive_recommendations.title: Mark up existing question-and-answer content with FAQPage schema
proactive_recommendations.rationale: The site already contains question-shaped content, but none of it is marked as FAQPage. FAQPage is the highest-leverage schema type for AI citation because its question/answer structure matches how retrieval systems chunk content and lift a quotable answer. The content already exists; only the markup is missing.

suggested_action.summary: Add FAQPage JSON-LD to pages that already answer common questions.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Wrap each question and its answer in FAQPage JSON-LD with mainEntity -> Question -> acceptedAnswer. Mark up the answers you already publish rather than writing new ones.

proactive_recommendations.title: Add BreadcrumbList schema to deep pages
proactive_recommendations.rationale: 1 crawled page(s) sit two or more levels deep with no BreadcrumbList markup. Breadcrumbs give both a visitor arriving cold from an AI answer and the assistant itself the parent context a deep URL otherwise lacks.

suggested_action.summary: Add BreadcrumbList JSON-LD alongside visible breadcrumb navigation.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Emit BreadcrumbList JSON-LD listing each ancestor with position, name and item URL, and render the same trail visibly at the top of the page.

proactive_recommendations.title: State AI usage terms explicitly in robots.txt
proactive_recommendations.rationale: robots.txt names which agents may crawl but says nothing about what may be done with the content once fetched. Emerging conventions -- Cloudflare's Content Signals Policy (released CC0) and RSL licensing terms -- let a publisher separate training use from search indexing and answer generation in machine-readable form, instead of leaving that distinction to be inferred from which user agents happen to be listed.

suggested_action.summary: Add machine-readable content-usage signals to robots.txt.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Add a Content Signals Policy block declaring your position on search, ai-input and ai-train separately, or publish RSL licensing terms. Keep it consistent with the agents you actually allow, or the two signals will contradict each other.

proactive_recommendations.title: Expose an agent-facing endpoint (NLWeb / MCP) built on existing structured data
proactive_recommendations.rationale: The site already publishes structured data, which is the input NLWeb uses to serve a conversational endpoint that AI agents can query directly rather than scraping HTML. Because it builds on schema.org markup, sitemaps and feeds you already maintain, it is incremental rather than a rebuild, and it moves the brand from being read by agents to being queryable by them.

suggested_action.summary: Evaluate an NLWeb instance exposing an /ask and /mcp endpoint over existing content.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Point an NLWeb instance at your existing schema.org data and sitemap, and expose /ask and /mcp. Start with the content an agent is most likely to be asked about -- catalogue, docs, pricing.
